what: A0 on its kinematic rungs (7c1's: arm_tracking writing the kinematic arm's joint positions, the motor's speed prescribed) against A0 on its dynamic rungs (A0Loops), both 0.3, float32, 10 s, at 1, 2, 3, 5, 7 and 10 Hz
crossing_rule: the declared line through zero, fitted against the window's largest commanded joint speed over 20 ms (speed_over_20_ms_max_window_rad_s); per step, the speed is the commands' rounding
read_with_it: the rung differences do not vanish with the commanded speed: the tracking error's is a fixed share, the joint loop's 20 ms trail against the controller's whole lag, so a line through zero places a crossing no run shows; above_the_threshold_at is what the runs show
conditions: the kinematic rung carries neither the rotor's axial reaction nor its gyroscopic torque, and has no spin-up kick: those are the dynamic rung's alone
A0 as declared: the magnet massless, the rotor's J 1e-5 kg m^2; the controller's filter 0.005 a tick, the tag's joint loop (Kp 1e4, Kd 200: a 20 ms trail) and rotor loop
the drag surrogate dejongh_mlp_v2 about the body's centre, 0.3's body step, dt 0.5 ms, float32

with_the_magnets_mass.what: A0 with the magnet's mass: density 7.5 g/cm^3 on motor.rotor (0.144 kg), J 2.59e-5 kg m^2 about the axis in all, top_speed 2 pi x 10 rad/s, the magnet's mass and mean inertia across the axis welded on link_6, its half difference across the axis (3.12e-6 kg m^2) carried as it turns; the joint loop reads the built tree with the magnet grafted
with_the_magnets_mass.inferences: both the magnet's spin about a diameter (its cylinder's axis along its moment, the rotor's x, spun about z) and its density are inferences (7a4's N1). If the physical magnet is diametrically magnetised and spun about its own axis, the rotor is symmetric about its axis (no half difference; J about the axis m r^2 / 2 = 2.2e-5 kg m^2 of the magnet), which is run beside it (magnet_axis along z)

restated_after_review.source: the review of PR #77 (its K4 and item 3), computed from this record's rows; restated, not re-measured

the_tracking_error_is_a_lag.reading: on both rungs the magnet trails the body by a lag times the swim speed: the kinematic rung by the controller's own 100 ms (its target filter's (1 - a)/a ticks and the one-step read), the dynamic rung by 19.5 ms more at every frequency, the joint servo's ramp-following lag (Kd/Kp = 20 ms, less about a step). So the +18.5 to +18.8 % is 19.5 ms over 100 ms, speed-invariant by construction: a relative measure of a speed-proportional quantity cannot shrink with the speed. The 20 ms is the 0.2 line's emulated servo gains, not a property of the AR4

restated_after_review.the_declared_crossing_rule: a line through zero of a relative rung difference against the commanded speed, crossing a relative threshold: it could not cross even the declaration's own prediction (18.60 and 18.79 %, a constant). It is kept as declared and does not describe these data
restated_after_review.the_rotation_rate_rows: the accumulator's and the slope estimator's, not a rung difference: at 1 and 2 Hz the kinematic motor's single-precision angle runs 5.4e-4 and 2.8e-4 fast (its increment rounded the same way every step), and at 3 to 10 Hz the motors' angle rates agree to 1.9e-6 while the rates fitted to the phase differ by 2.7e-5 to 7.3e-5 (a field whose turning is less even). #99 does not cite them (MIME-ANO-124)
restated_after_review.for_99: the kinematic rung's validity line needs (a) a lag (or bandwidth) condition, the joint servo's ramp lag against the controller's, (b) an absolute tolerance on the end effector's pose: the magnet's position error is v x 19.5 ms, which crosses an absolute tolerance at a speed, where against the comparison's relative tolerance (7e-4 on the tracking error) the kinematic rung stands in for this dynamic one at no speed; and (c) the watch on commanded joint speeds and accelerations against the description's limits as a separate guard, which this data cannot earn (the commands reach 0.92 % of the limit at most). Recorded as data for a1, not built. The line earned here is relative to the 0.2 line's assumed servo
restated_after_review.the_wrist_kick: a bare-wrist artefact, which #99 must not cite as an arm's behaviour: the AR4 description has no armature, no transmission and no joint dynamics, and its motor links are massless (the build warns), so the rotor's spin-up (J 1e-5 kg m^2, 4.1 times link 6's inertia about its axis) turns the bare wrist. The review's two-degree-of-freedom hand model (joint 6 under the computed-torque loop, the rotor under the PI, nothing else) gives 0.5105 rad and 33.05 rad/s at 10 Hz and 0.1532 rad, 9.914 rad/s at 3 Hz, as the runs do: joint 6 at 2.1 to 21 times its limit. A geared joint's reflected inertia (an armature) would hold it inside the limit; a separate phase builds it
